A.summary: The strongest power distribution and a well-referenced CM4 USB pair make A a close second. Overlapping Ethernet tuning copper hides real path skew, and the flash data routing and USB-C launch add avoidable transitions.

B.summary: The 29 missing connections include the 1.2 V converter switch node and RP2040 USB data. Bottom-side PCIe routes cross large gaps in the power planes, and the inner ground fill reaches the routed outline.

C.summary: Local switch-node pours, ground stitching and top-side flash routing are strengths. Lane 3 has substantial receive-pair skew, the saved stack gives poor impedance estimates, and refill leaves 19 zone-intersection errors.

D.summary: D is the best release candidate, with credible impedance geometry, matched Ethernet paths and short top-side flash routes. The long 0.60 mm fan supply, local return discontinuities and assembly details still need sign-off.

human_guess.why: C combines individually shaped switch-node pours, local pad-level fill keepouts, ground stitching and curved skew tuning in particular PCIe corridors. The combination looks like repeated local decisions made in the PCB editor. Authorship remains an inference.
